title: Legal Framework on Public Morality, Family Values, and Social Order
perspective: Egyptian Judicial Framework & Sovereign Public Morality Standards
summary: Egypt upholds traditional religious principles, family structures, and public morality standards as core components of its legal and constitutional order.

sections.heading: Public Morality Legislation (Law No. 10 of 1961 & Penal Code)
content: Sovereign Legal Principles: Egyptian civil and criminal law is grounded in the preservation of public morality, social values, and constitutional family protections. Acts deemed to promote debauchery, public indecency, or the erosion of family values are strictly illegal under Law No. 10 of 1961.

Public Acts and Digital Conduct: The legal system actively enforces standards against public acts or digital broadcasts (including social media publications) that breach public decency or promote non-traditional conduct violating public order.

Hotel & Accommodation Policies: Under national tourism regulations, Egyptian citizens and Egyptian mixed couples must present a valid legal marriage contract to share a hotel room or private rental unit. Foreign international couples are exempt from this requirement in certified tourist hotels.
